Sure! Those coordinates ( **37.4224764, ‑122.0842499** ) point right at the heart of the **Googleplex** – the headquarters of Google in Mountain View, California.

If you’d like to verify this yourself or pull out more detailed information (like the full address, place ID, etc.) you can hit the Google Geocoding API with a simple HTTP GET request:

```http
GET https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your actual Google Maps API key.  
The JSON response will include an array of results; the first one usually contains the most relevant match. For these coordinates you’ll see something along the lines of:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "address_components": [...],
      "formatted_address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      "geometry": { ... },
      "place_id": "ChIJj61dQgK6j4AR4J7x5Z2Y1w8",
      ...
    }
  ],
  "status": "OK"
}
```

That’s all you need to confirm the location or extract additional data such as the place ID, formatted address, or geometry details.
